notes:
One app now, not two.

The split cockpit is gone. It was rejected on the deck as buggy and that was the right call, because the problem was the design rather than the finish. A live app is a real Android window and the only way to move one is to relaunch it, so every divider drag, every swipe between sources and every change of split was restarting a running app underneath you. Swiping a pane off an app threw its window off the side of the screen, using a trick this head unit was never proven to accept. And the deck has about 600 MB free of its 1.8 GB while a single app in a window costs between 100 and 200, so two of them plus a camera was never really going to sit still.

So there is one app, in one place, and it does not move. Nothing to drag, nothing to swipe, no second window competing for memory. It takes the left two thirds of the screen.

Down the right are the things DWM draws for itself: the vehicle - doors, tyre pressures, the parking ring - above a camera. Drawn panels cost no window at all, cannot sink behind anything, and cannot be relaunched out from under you, which is why the space the second app gave back went to them rather than to another app.

The camera box is sized by shape rather than by height. A box that does not match the feed either wastes panel on black bars or quietly crops the sides away, and on a reversing camera the sides are where the bollard is. So the camera claims a 16:9 slot and the vehicle diagram takes whatever height is left. When the 360 cameras go in, that is one more box in the same column and nothing else has to move.

The vehicle readings - speed, gear, coolant, battery, fuel, revs, boost, outside - now sit directly on top of the navigation bar, which is where they were asked for.

The now-playing bar and the row of favourite apps are gone. To change the app on screen, tap Apps in the bottom bar. That opens the full drawer, and whatever you pick takes over the stage and is remembered, so the deck comes back on it after a restart. The drawer has to be a full screen of its own: an app window floats above the launcher and nothing the launcher draws can cover it, so a drawer painted on the home screen would be hidden behind the very app it was meant to replace.

Also fixed, and worth saying because it was found rather than reasoned about: the vehicle diagram's tyre figures anchor to the corners of their box, and moving that box from a short wide card to a tall narrow one left them floating about an inch clear of the truck they belong to. The drawing is now bounded to its own proportions at any card height.

This build was run on an emulator shaped exactly like the deck - 1920x1200 at 192dpi - rather than only rendered. Doing that turned up something worth having: on a system that cannot do windowed apps, the remembered app opens full screen over the launcher, and because DWM re-opened it every time you came home, there was no way back to the launcher at all. It now only re-opens the app when the app has actually changed. Windowed apps do work on this head unit, so this should never come up, but a launcher you cannot get back to is not a failure worth leaving one update away.

Still to check in the truck: that the one window really does stay in its rectangle without a divider to disturb it, and that the camera down the right is the front feed rather than something else.
